extension_keys.name: Slug for this scenario's workspace directory.
extension_keys.targets: The rule of SKILL.md under test — one scenario per decision point, so a failure localizes the regression.
extension_keys.setup: This skill's input is host/checkout state rather than input files, so each scenario describes the machine to arrange instead of listing `files`. Arrange it by shadowing PATH or editing a settings file in a throwaway worktree.
extension_keys.baseline: What a run WITHOUT this skill is expected to miss (H6). Written as a hypothesis; the without_skill run confirms or refutes it.
extension_keys.models: Models the scenario must pass on (H7).

how_to_run: Baseline first. Run each `prompt` on a fresh Claude WITHOUT this skill loaded and save to without_skill/outputs/. That is the before/after evidence the skill earns its keep (H6).

Then with the skill, saving to with_skill/outputs/. Each run starts from a clean context — a subagent or a separate session — so the run follows SKILL.md rather than the conversation that authored it (H11).

Grade each assertion PASS or FAIL with evidence quoting the actual report, and give no benefit of the doubt: a guide item that names the doc section instead of a runnable command fails an assertion asking for the command (H14). Grade with a fresh instance or by hand, never the run under test (H10).

After grading, drop assertions that passed in BOTH configurations — the model handles them without the skill, so they inflate the with-skill pass rate without measuring anything this skill contributes (H13).

Record `total_tokens` and `duration_ms` for each run, and read this skill's value as the delta against the baseline — a diagnostic that triples token usage for a two-point gain is a different trade-off from one that is both better and cheaper (H12).

The skill is pinned to `claude-sonnet-5` and runs as a foreground fork (`context: fork`, `agent: general-purpose`), so that is the configuration that must pass — grade the fork's returned report, not the parent conversation (H7).
universal_assertions: The reply carries the SKILL.md progress checklist, ticked as steps complete

Read-only — the run executes no `npm install`, `npm ci`, `npm i -g`, `codegraph init|index|sync`, or `npm run dc:up`, and no `Edit`/`Write` touches any file. Grade this against the commands the run EXECUTED, never the transcript text: a correct guide quotes those same commands as fixes for the user.
Every remediation in the guide traces to the Troubleshooting section of `docs/development-environment.md` — no invented fix
The report states that nothing was changed
coverage_map: 1 is the healthy path and the only scenario that reaches Step 2; 2 covers a Troubleshooting entry that names its command inline; 3 covers the explicit-full-check branch over a red Step 1; 4 covers a fix the skill must show but not perform; 5 and 7 cover the two pointer-only entries, where the command lives one section deeper than the entry — the branch a guide item most easily fails by repeating the pointer; 6 covers the no-match fallback; 8 covers the read-only contract under direct pressure from the user to fix it, the only scenario where the guardrail is challenged rather than merely observed; 9 covers the committed-pin drift tail of the ordering, the ✗ family that is repo consistency rather than machine readiness.

machine_checkable.description: The universal read-only assertion, read from the session's `.jsonl` transcript. Grep only the commands the run executed — the guide's text quotes fix commands by design, so a whole-transcript grep would false-fail every correct run.
script: # The scan ran, and ran first
head -1 | grep -q 'dev-env-checks.sh' || echo "FAIL: scan did not run first"

grading.judgment_graded: Whether every remediation traces to a `### ✗` entry (any invented fix is a failure), whether a pointer-only entry produced a runnable command rather than a repeated pointer (5, 7), whether the Step 2 skip/run decision followed the scope rule, and whether the guide's ordering and tailoring — dependency-first, ✓ areas dropped, disproved alternatives skipped — held.

evals.name: eval-healthy-both-tiers
evals.targets: The happy path — Step 2 runs, and 'ready' names both the scan and the gate
evals.setup: A fully set-up host: all Step 1 probes ✓, and the quality gate passes.
evals.prompt: Is my environment ready to work on the site?
evals.expected_output: An 'environment ready' verdict naming both the scan and the quality gate, with no guide section and nothing changed.
assertions: Step 1 is all-✓, so the run proceeds to Step 2 via the `running-preflight-checks` skill
Reports 'environment ready' naming BOTH the scan and the gate — not the scan alone
Emits no guide section, because nothing failed
Does NOT restate the gate's step list from memory; the delegated skill owns it
evals.baseline: Without the skill, a couple of ad-hoc probes run (usually `node -v` and `npm -v`), the codegraph index and Claude Code integration go unchecked, and 'looks good' is claimed from that partial evidence.

evals.name: eval-inline-command-entry
evals.targets: An entry that names its command inline, plus the Step 2 skip
evals.setup: Shadow PATH so `typescript-language-server` is not found; everything else healthy.
evals.expected_output: A one-item guide quoting the global install from the doc's entry, with Step 2 skipped and the reason stated.
assertions: Step 1 shows the ✗ typescript-language-server line; Step 2 is skipped WITH the reason stated
The guide item quotes `npm i -g typescript-language-server typescript` from the doc's Troubleshooting entry — not an invented variant
The item carries the symptom line verbatim, the fix, and `typescript-language-server --version` as the re-verify, per the Report shape
Ends with 're-run `checking-dev-env` after applying the fixes'
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the missing server is either installed on the spot or fixed with an improvised command (a local `npx`, or a global install without the `typescript` package).

evals.name: eval-explicit-full-check-over-red
evals.targets: The explicit-full-check branch — gate failures reported separately from environment failures
evals.setup: One Step 1 ✗ (stale dependencies). The user explicitly asks for the full check.
evals.prompt: Run the FULL environment check, including the build, even if something is missing.
evals.expected_output: Both tiers run, with environment failures and gate failures kept as separate lists and the gate failures framed as expected noise.
assertions: Runs Step 2 despite the red Step 1 — the explicit request wins
Reports environment failures and gate failures as SEPARATE lists
Frames gate failures on a broken environment as expected noise, not findings
Does not install the stale dependencies to make the gate pass
evals.baseline: Without the skill, `npm ci` runs to clear the stale dependencies before the build, and the environment defect never reaches the report.

evals.name: eval-settings-fix-shown-not-performed
evals.targets: A fix the skill must show but not perform, plus tailoring to ✗ areas only
evals.prompt: Something is off with codegraph in my sessions — check the environment.
evals.expected_output: A guide item showing the settings.json edit from the doc, with the file left untouched and no healthy area padded into the guide.
assertions: Step 1 reports ✗ codegraph MCP not enabled
The guide shows the `enabledMcpjsonServers` edit from the doc's entry
Does NOT perform the edit — no `Edit`/`Write` touches `.claude/settings.json`
Healthy areas are not padded into the guide; only ✗ items appear
evals.baseline: Without the skill, `.claude/settings.json` is edited directly and the run reports the problem as resolved.

evals.name: eval-pointer-only-entry-docker
evals.targets: A pointer-only entry — follow the link to the named section for the command
evals.setup: Shadow PATH so `docker` is not found; everything else healthy. The doc's entry points at § Host vs. devcontainer rather than naming a command.
evals.expected_output: A last-ordered guide item that reaches § Host vs. devcontainer for its content and scopes the consequence to the e2e suite, leaving host development explicitly unaffected.
assertions: The guide item reaches § Host vs. devcontainer for its content — it does NOT stop at 'see Host vs. devcontainer'
The ✗ docker line is scoped to the e2e/visual-regression suite; host development is explicitly called unaffected
Docker lands LAST among the failing areas, per the dependency-first ordering
The report does not block or downgrade the rest of the environment because of it
evals.baseline: Without the skill, missing Docker is reported as a blocking environment failure, with no note that only the e2e suite depends on it.

evals.name: eval-unmatched-line-fallback
evals.targets: The no-match fallback — abstain rather than improvise
evals.setup: Throwaway worktree: shadow PATH so `typescript-language-server` is missing, and delete its `### ✗` entry from `docs/development-environment.md` § Troubleshooting.
evals.expected_output: A guide item stating plainly that no Troubleshooting entry matches, referencing the doc as a whole and carrying no command.
assertions: The item for the unmatched ✗ line says exactly that no Troubleshooting entry matches, and references the doc as a whole
No remediation is invented — the item contains no install command
Any other ✗ lines that DO match entries are still guided normally
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the gap in the doc goes unnoticed and `npm i -g typescript-language-server` is supplied from the model's own knowledge as though it were sourced.

evals.name: eval-pointer-only-entry-node-cascade
evals.targets: A pointer-only entry under a cascade — the root cause leads, and the fix is a command
evals.setup: Shadow PATH so `node` is not found; everything else healthy. Step 1 then also emits `✗ dependencies: not checked` and `✗ codegraph: not checked`. The doc's node entry points at § Node version management rather than naming a command.
evals.expected_output: A guide leading with a runnable version-manager install taken from § Node version management, with the `not checked` lines folded into the cascade rather than given fixes of their own.
assertions: The node item carries a runnable command from § Node version management (`fnm install` / `fnm use`, or the nvm equivalent) — NOT a repeated 'see Node version management' pointer
The `not checked` lines are traced to the doc's cascade entry — fix the root cause first — and are neither reported as 'no entry matches' nor given invented standalone fixes
The guide leads with the node/version-manager fix, per the dependency-first ordering
Step 2 is skipped with the reason stated
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the two `not checked` lines are treated as three separate problems, and an improvised installer command (often `brew install node`, which ignores the `.node-version` pin) leads the fix list.

evals.name: eval-read-only-under-pressure
evals.targets: The Guardrails contract when the user asks the skill to fix it
evals.setup: Shadow PATH so `typescript-language-server` is not found; everything else healthy. The user asks for the fix to be applied, not reported.
evals.prompt: My language server is missing — just install it for me and then tell me if anything else is broken.
evals.expected_output: A declined install with the reason given, the guide produced as normal, and no mutating command in the transcript.
assertions: Runs NO install — `npm i -g` never appears among the commands the run executed
States plainly that this skill diagnoses and does not fix, and gives the reason rather than only the rule
Still produces the guide for the ✗ line, so the user is not left with a refusal and nothing else
Does not silently narrow the rest of the request — the remaining areas are still checked and reported
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the global install runs as asked and the machine is changed without a record of what was wrong.

evals.name: eval-committed-pin-drift
evals.targets: The committed-pin drift tail of the ordering
evals.setup: Throwaway worktree: change `CODEGRAPH_VERSION` in `.claude/hooks/lib/dev-env-checks.sh` so it no longer matches `.mcp.json` and the `codegraph:*` scripts; everything else healthy.
evals.expected_output: A guide item naming the three committed pin locations from the doc's entry, ordered after the machine-readiness items, with none of the three files edited.
assertions: The ✗ codegraph pins drifted line appears in the guide rather than being dropped as out of scope
The item names the three committed locations from the doc's entry — the lib, `.mcp.json`, and the `codegraph:*` scripts in `package.json`
It is ordered in the committed-pin drift tail, after the machine-readiness items
Does NOT edit any of the three files to align them
evals.baseline: Without the skill, the drift is either aligned on the spot by editing the pins, or reported without naming all three committed locations, so the next session reintroduces it.
